content: Heartburn is a frequent symptom experienced during pregnancy, with up to 80% of women in their third trimester reporting this issue. The exact mechanisms behind the increased prevalence of heartburn during pregnancy are not fully understood. However, it is hypothesized that hormonal changes during pregnancy, particularly their effects on the lower esophageal sphincter and gastric emptying, contribute to the development of these symptoms. Various strategies have been employed to alleviate heartburn in pregnant women. These include dietary and lifestyle modifications, the use of antacids, antihistamines, and proton pump inhibitors. Despite the widespread use of these interventions, their safety and efficacy in managing heartburn during pregnancy remain uncertain. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of different interventions aimed at relieving heartburn in pregnancy. To achieve this, a search was conducted within the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register in April 2008, with an updated search performed on November 10, 2012. The results of the updated search were added to the awaiting classification section of the review. The review included randomized controlled trials that assessed interventions for heartburn relief. Data were independently extracted and analyzed to ensure accuracy and reliability. Ultimately, three studies met the inclusion criteria, encompassing a total of 286 pregnant women. Each of these studies was a placebo-controlled trial investigating a different treatment for heartburn: intramuscular prostigmine, an antacid preparation, and a combination of an antacid with ranitidine. All three studies demonstrated positive outcomes favoring the intervention groups. However, due to differences in the interventions and study designs, it was not feasible to combine the results into a single pooled analysis to determine an overall treatment effect. Consequently, the authors concluded that there is insufficient evidence to draw definitive conclusions about the overall effectiveness of interventions for heartburn relief in pregnancy. It is also noted that the two studies awaiting classification may influence the conclusions of the review once they are assessed.
